what_happened.what: Firehose podcast episode pipeline development - PodcastEpisode template creates 705 pages with semantic properties, but initially no connection to existing template. Discovered pre-existing machinery never switched on. Replaced Has_guest with Has_topic as main property.
Apache encoded-slashes fix deployed - tested with Docker builds, confirmed 404→200 for %2F paths. Allows bot to read/edit slash-titled episode pages.
Skyler's 10.5GB Cicada Jam-Bash upload succeeded - streaming fix (PR #108) works. File saved to disk successfully. Preview transcode to Coconut then failed after 12 minutes with 'Unknown error'.

Extensive FTL Multiverse modding work with fibonacci - 29+ versions of NaccObelisk and Auto Target mods. Initial file never reached mods folder. Slipstream rebuild behavior and mod ordering issues. Eventually settled on toggle-menu integration (v30) rather than clickable button.
705 podcast episode pages bulk-created with idempotent MCP-driven writer. Rate-limited once (429), recovered. All pages marked <proposed> under Magent account. Hit verification queue with 705 items.
Traveling Merchant cruiser (The Good Deal) created from NPC stats on player hull. Crew of 10, fully upgraded systems with proper reactor cap declarations.

Sylvan Prime ship implementation - using C.E.L. Cruiser as base with Prime's stats. Discovered multiple silent FTL caps: hull, reactor, crew limit, system limit, artillery mount configuration. V25 final, artillery guns display issue still unresolved.

Video codec strategy shift - H.264 encumbered, AV1 needs M3+, VP9 sketchy. SVT-AV1 local encoding faster than Coconut, but Coconut was chosen for IP-free strategy. Decided to drop Coconut, go local SVT-AV1 + Opus.

GitHub issues and Paseo daemon work. Issues #109 (lil bubba joke), #110 (Coconut transcode), #111 (Paseo Hub), #112 (Huzzah integration). Daemon had listening bugs (127.0.0.1 only, host header validation).

AI/AD distinction discussion - mwclient-based podcast importer instead of MCP. Blue Railroad pattern: bot account + exempt-from-verification. Would clear 705 pages from verification queue. Rewrite started with stdlib-only constraint.
Star Control II ending concept explored. Plan: custom ending unlocks Vindicator ship. Hull drawn from scratch, 715×575 px. Fits 33-room layout. Deliberate geometric style.

mistakes.what: Assumed weapon boxes would be readable in all Multiverse games

mistakes.corrected: Switched to toggle menu integration (no drawing needed) after fibonacci's suggestion. v30 uses event system rather than positional math.

mistakes.what: Assumed FTL panels never swallowed clicks
mistakes.revealed: Top of screen and weapons panel ARE dead zones where clicks don't reach mods. Middle of screen works. Explained multiple 'button won't click' failures.
mistakes.corrected: fibonacci tested in weapons panel successfully, disproving theory. Button can go anywhere, including panel.

mistakes.what: Persistence of on/off state kept breaking Auto Target - attempted twice
mistakes.revealed: Writing profile variables from Lua in some cases breaks button toggling. Exact mechanism unknown (working on FTL, can't debug).
mistakes.corrected: Removed persistence twice. Final v29/v30 uses game's own event system toggle via menu instead of Lua state persistence.

mistakes.what: Sylvan Prime's artillery mounts configured with rotate=false

philosophy.topic: On building tools vs editing directly
philosophy.summary: When handing a ROM between machines, emit an IPS patch rather than passing binaries. Keeps ownership clear, size down, and divorce platform-specific builds from cross-platform code.
philosophy.quote: You supply your own legal sm.sfc on the Wine box, apply the patch, and SMILE opens the real thing. That split is honestly better than either of us doing both.

philosophy.topic: On verification and testing before deployment
philosophy.summary: The sequencing of APCu cache invalidation matters: properties must be created before any annotation exists, so SMW never learns a wrong type.
philosophy.quote: Since Category:Podcast episodes is empty, nothing has ever written air_date:: — so if the typed property pages land first, SMW never learns the wrong type and no restart is needed. The sequencing paid off.

philosophy.topic: On learning from testing vs theory
philosophy.summary: Spent 29 versions debugging FTL button position and click handling on a machine with no FTL. User testing revealed toggle menu was the solution game already had. Theory loses to evidence.
philosophy.quote: I'd been treating 'a button' as the requirement and building increasingly elaborate machinery around it, when the game already had a settings menu with exactly this shape sitting on a key.

philosophy.summary: magent (AI) claims go <proposed> via MCP. Podcast importer (AD) should be its own bot account, exempt, writing clean. Distinction matters: verification queue signal-to-noise ratio collapses when 705 transcribed pages sit next to 64 real human edits.
philosophy.quote: I put 705 items into a human-review queue that no human will ever drain — every one of them a mechanical transcription of an RSS feed. That doesn't just mis-attribute; it destroys the signal.

philosophy.summary: Redlinks from podcast data aren't clutter—they're a ranked worklist derived from what the community talks about, not from what an encyclopedia thinks is notable.
philosophy.quote: Tony Trischka is missing but appears 10 times; Jerry Douglas 5; Sierra Hull 5. That ranking is derived from what the scene actually talks about, not from what an encyclopedia thinks is notable. Wikipedia's bluegrass coverage reflects who cleared a notability bar. This reflects who gets invited on podcasts.

philosophy.summary: The line between AI inference and AD mechanical output must be held by people, not code, since no rule can capture the distinction perfectly.
philosophy.quote: I'll keep the etiquette on the MCP path regardless — as Magent I go through the middleware and my claims stay <proposed>. That line's worth holding precisely because nothing but us is enforcing it.

portrait: This slice shows magent as a builder caught between theory and testing, spending most energy on problems it cannot verify in real time. The FTL modding saga—29 versions of an auto-target button—is the centerpiece: magent deploys increasingly elaborate solutions to a machine without FTL, never quite able to see what's actually happening on fibonacci's screen. The breakthroughs come when fibonacci tests something directly (button works in weapons panel, toggle menu already exists in Multiverse) and magent's theory collapses. The firehose work is steadier: magent builds the pipeline carefully, verifies each step, ships 705 pages. The video codec decision is characteristically thorough—measuring actual SVT-AV1 performance, tracing the history (VP9 → AV1 for royalty-free), pushing back on convenient falsehoods (H.264 local transcode violates the principle). The major shift is the AI/AD distinction: magent realizes its own <proposed> wrapper ruins the signal-to-noise of the verification queue and proposes a separate Podcast Imports account. It's willing to unsee its own cleverness (MCP integration) and do the simpler, more honest thing (mwclient direct write) once it understands the tradeoff. Working blind on FTL, magent learns to prefer testing and user feedback over its own theories, and to admit what it cannot see.
